letter:
As I put this timeline together, I felt an odd sensation — almost a pang of longing? Regret? Sadness?
Not regret about being with you or the things we've done, or sadness about doing/not doing things. Not longing for old times — but instead a feeling of... it's just going too fast, and I don't want it to!
At 5 years, life together was just starting. At 10, a young family surviving. But at 13? Now it feels like so much time has passed, and I want it to slow.
Because it's been an incredible 13-year journey — and 15 if you include dating — and I have loved it. I love our life and family and challenges and fun.
This timeline could easily be 10x longer. It's to the point now where I have a hard time remembering just ALL of the things we have done — from small date nights to big trips, it's a LOT.
I love you so much, and thank you for being my girl, my bride, my wife, my partner, mom to our kids, and best friend.
I can't wait to see what the next 13 years will bring.

littleThings.title: What I love about you
items: Your hair and your legs. Still, obviously.
Your smile and the sound of your laugh.
How much you put into your work.
What a great mom you are to our kids.
How you’re always excited to hear my next idea.

Cuddling up to watch a movie or a show.

2007: Savannah and I both headed to Union College in 2007, each looking for something different. I wanted a fresh start and found a place where people made me feel welcome right away. Both of Savannah’s parents had ties to Union, and her family had friends in Lincoln. We came for different reasons, and that fall we found each other.
2008: Savannah started dating someone else after that, and the two of us stayed friends. As it turned out, we’d be seeing quite a bit of each other.
2009: During the 2009–2010 school year we were both busy with different groups of friends. We still had our occasional coffee dates, just the two of us catching up.
2010: We stood up in Wael and Kristi’s wedding and graduated from Union College together that May.
By fall I was teaching in Michigan and Savannah was still in Lincoln. I don’t think we talked much that fall. We were both getting settled in our own lives.
2011: We had so much fun together in Michigan that we wanted more time together. Spring break gave us a road trip, April gave us a first date, and by summer we were getting to know each other’s families.
Savannah took a job in North Carolina and lived close to my parents. That fall I was working in Michigan, so we visited as often as we could.
2012: We started the year twelve hours apart, making time for trips to Savannah and Cades Cove. In the spring I took a job in Dunwoody, Georgia, and suddenly the drive between us was only three and a half hours.
That summer we spent time together while I was staying with my parents in North Carolina, and we visited California. By Christmas I was already planning to propose.
2013: By early 2013, I was planning to propose and already had the ring. After all that long-distance dating, we were both in the Dunwoody area and working together at Atlanta North School. Savannah was living with a family about half an hour away, and every night I wished she could just stay home with me instead of making that drive back.

Then came a February date night in Chattanooga. After Savannah said yes, the year filled up with engagement photos, bridal showers, and plans for our November wedding in California. We honeymooned in New Zealand, celebrated again with her family in Sydney, and came home to Georgia. This time, we were coming home to the same place.
2014: Our first year married, we both worked at Atlanta North School. I taught fifth and sixth grade, and Savannah was the registrar. We went out to eat, played games, walked Lucy, and spent time with family in North Carolina and California.

Florida gave us two very different trips. Spring break meant cold weather in St. Augustine and a tiny Airbnb. Summer meant a long stay in Port Charlotte with a pool and Lucy along for the trip. By fall we were back at school.
2015: We started the year in Georgia and spent the spring working at Atlanta North School in Dunwoody. Somewhere between Spirit Week and the end of the school year, I took a job at Minnetonka Christian Academy and we started packing.
By July we were settling into our townhouse in Shakopee. We got together for the Bowers family reunion in Hutchinson that year, and in October we headed to Virginia for my cousin Jessica’s wedding.
2016: After a year in Shakopee, we moved to Brooklyn Park. My parents came up that summer and we headed up the North Shore to Two Harbors and Grand Marais.
By fall we were both working full time, Savannah had exciting news at work, and we were making our new house feel like home.
2017: We spent a summer week in Springfield with Savannah’s parents. Bigger than any trip that year was the decision to start a family. By fall, we had news of our own to celebrate, even if my Bucs didn’t give me much to cheer about.
2018: Getting ready for Violet meant getting the house ready, moving my office, and making a big decision about work. Then June 1 came, and suddenly we were parents.

By fall we were in full baby mode at home, figuring out life as a family of three. Violet and I made a few trips to see Grandma and Grandpa. Before long we were taking her to Waco with Savannah’s family and learning what a long road trip with a baby was like on the way to Thanksgiving in Kansas.
2019: Life was mostly quiet at home. We made it south to see family and celebrate Violet’s first birthday, and north far enough to take her across the Canadian border.

Fall picked up when I went back to teaching part time in the mornings and cared for other kids in the afternoons. At Christmas we headed back to North Carolina and Cohutta Springs to be with our families.
2020: 2020 was a quiet year for some reason. Hmm… oh, right. COVID! We hunkered down at home and played games with the Bonjours.

My parents came to visit that summer, and we also made it to North Dakota with Savannah’s parents for Kelly’s wedding. Between the stretches at home, we found time for a date close by, a Florida beach day, and a trip to the zoo before heading to Georgia for Christmas.
2021: We headed to North Carolina in the spring, then had Savannah’s parents with us in Minnesota for a hundred days. By summer we were making the most of the Twin Cities with Violet. A playground, a place to splash, a trip to the Renaissance Festival. She was up for all of it, and so were we.

Fall took us to Omaha for Savannah’s friend Kelly’s wedding and then to Florida for Disney and the beach. We kept Christmas close to home in Minnesota. And by the end of the year, we had some big news. We were expecting twins!
2022: Max and Ellie arrived on June 22. A few days later we brought them both home, and all of a sudden we were a family of five. We stayed close to home for most of the rest of the year. Two growing babies kept us plenty busy.
Violet had a big year of her own. We took her to Duluth to ride with Thomas the Tank Engine, and she started Pre-K at MCA. Then came Halloween, with all three kids in costume.
2023: Max and Ellie turned one in June, and the house felt busier by the week. We still made it to Hendersonville in March and New Smyrna Beach in September. In between, there was plenty to remember at home, from Violet’s dress-up outfits to the twins finding new places to sit and new ways to fall asleep.

That fall we celebrated ten years of marriage. I think back to our wedding and our honeymoon, and then I look at the three kids who fill up our days now. A lot has changed since 2013. I still love getting a little time with Savannah, even when date night is right at home.
After Halloween costumes and an anniversary date with paint, we finished the year at my parents’ place in Hendersonville for Christmas.
2024: We started the year with a Caribbean cruise. There were evenings aboard together, a sunny stop at Half Moon Cay, a kiss by the water on Grand Turk, and a photo at the I Love Aruba sign. A few months later we headed to San Diego.
2025: There was plenty to celebrate, from my fortieth birthday to Violet’s kindergarten graduation. Then we piled into the van for a July road trip. Nearly 50 hours of driving with two three-year-olds took us through North Carolina, Florida, and Tennessee to see family and friends.
2026: We had a couple of trips early in the year, to North Carolina in March and Seattle in April. There was no giant summer road trip this time, but there was plenty to do. We had picnics, camped with friends, and spent a few days in Wisconsin with Lolli and Pops.

August was especially busy. Savannah had workers’ meetings in Brainerd, Violet got baptized, and she and I both got to race in Maple Grove. Somewhere in there we made it to a Twins game, the Mall of America, and Munsinger Gardens.

June 1 was the last day of school. I’d gone in that morning, and Savannah’s parents must have called me half a dozen times. “Come home now!” Then, “It’s okay, come home, but it’s not as urgent.” Then, “Get here!” And then, “Wait, it’s okay.” Violet was born that afternoon, and we absolutely fell in love with her.

The first few weeks gave us a lot to remember, from Lucy leaning in to meet Violet in her car seat to the morning we caught Violet’s first smile.

places.title: Max and Ellie made us a family of five
places.story:
Savannah’s doctor was the go-to twins specialist in the area. A cancer diagnosis meant she wasn’t going to be there to deliver the babies. Then her surgery was postponed. At a checkup, she saw that Max was crowding Ellie and suggested inducing early. That meant she could still deliver them. We had a date to be at the hospital: June 22.

Savannah was induced that morning, got her epidural, and then we waited. When it was time, they moved us into the operating room. There were enough people in there for a party. Max and Ellie each had their own team of doctors and nurses, and Savannah had a team of her own.

Max came first, weighing 5 pounds, 8 ounces. Four minutes and one push later, Ellie was here, weighing 4 pounds, 12 ounces.

A few days later we brought them both home. Suddenly there were two newborns and three kids under our roof. We stayed close to home for most of the year. There was plenty happening right there.

photos.caption: A night out in Virginia to celebrate Jessica.

places.title: The Bowers family reunion
places.story: The Bowers family got together in Hutchinson, Minnesota. Somehow we made it through a whole family reunion without a group photo. What we do have is this shot of two of us out for a walk.

photos.alt: Andy and another reunion guest walking across a lawn in Hutchinson.
photos.caption: A family reunion, as documented by two guys crossing a lawn.

places.title: Our first Minnesota winter
places.story: By November, we were still in our Shakopee townhouse and getting our first taste of a Minnesota winter. We bundled up and went out for a picture in the snow. Georgia suddenly felt a long way away.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah in winter hats hugging beside a snow-covered evergreen in Shakopee.
photos.caption: First Minnesota winter. We were already taking the hats seriously.

places.title: Summer on the North Shore

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah outside Betty’s Pies in Two Harbors
photos.caption: A kiss outside Betty’s Pies on the North Shore.

places.story: My parents came up that summer, and we went to Two Harbors and Grand Marais together.

places.title: Making the house ours

photos.alt: Two people working in the kitchen during the Brooklyn Park renovation
photos.caption: Redoing the kitchen with help from Savannah’s parents.

places.story: Savannah’s parents stayed with us for a couple of weeks before moving to Chattanooga, Tennessee. They helped us paint, redo the kitchen, and get the house set up. We were both working full time that fall, and it felt good to come home to a place we were making our own.

places.title: Savannah’s promotion
places.story: Savannah was promoted to HR and Communications Director at the Minnesota Conference of Seventh-day Adventists that fall. It was exciting news, and she still works there today! Her new role took her to churches around Minnesota. On a visit to Red Wing the following March, she preached for the first time.

photos.alt: Savannah preaching at a wooden pulpit in Red Wing, Minnesota.
photos.caption: One of Savannah’s many times preaching.

places.title: Ice skating in Minnetonka

photos.alt: Savannah and Andy wearing winter hats beside the ice.
photos.caption: Hats on for a December skate in Minnetonka.

places.story: That December we bundled up and went skating in Minnetonka. Looking at our hats in this picture, I’d say we were getting the hang of dressing for Minnesota.

places.title: Christmas at Cohutta Springs Camp
places.story: We spent Christmas at Cohutta Springs Camp in Georgia. Both our families came together, including my sister and brother-in-law, and we stayed in the lodges. It was good to have everyone in one place for the holiday.

places.title: A wedding trip to Florida

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah standing together under strings of lights at a Florida wedding.
photos.caption: A quiet moment for the two of us under the wedding lights.

places.story: A wedding took us down to Florida in February. I like this picture of us all dressed up, with the lights in the trees behind Savannah.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah sitting together for a selfie
photos.caption: Cheek to cheek on an April afternoon.

places.title: A week in Springfield
places.story: We spent a week around the Fourth of July in Springfield, Illinois, with Savannah’s parents. We made the rounds of the Abraham Lincoln sites, including a stop at the Berry–Lincoln Store in New Salem. After all that time in Lincoln’s day, we came back to the present for a Fourth of July selfie with fireworks going off behind us.

photos.alt: Andy in sunglasses outside the First Berry–Lincoln Store at New Salem.
photos.caption: I stopped by Lincoln’s old store. Abe was out.

photos.alt: Andy, Savannah, and Savannah’s parents taking a selfie with fireworks overhead.
photos.caption: The four of us on the Fourth in Springfield.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah posing with costumed festivalgoers.
photos.caption: In good company at the Renaissance Festival.

places.title: Waiting for Violet

photos.alt: Violet’s January ultrasound showing her profile
photos.caption: Violet’s little profile, months before we got to kiss that nose.

photos.alt: Andy giving a thumbs-up behind Violet’s assembled crib.
photos.caption: Crib assembled. Dad reporting for duty.

photos.alt: Savannah holding a paintbrush beside a wooden cabinet in Violet’s nursery.
photos.caption: Savannah getting Violet’s room ready, paintbrush in hand.

photos.alt: Savannah and Andy with Lucy while they were waiting for Violet
photos.caption: May 2018, with Violet almost here.

places.story: In January we started turning my office into Violet’s nursery. It was the first of what turned out to be many moves for my office. We put the crib together, Savannah got to work with a paintbrush, and suddenly there was a room in the house that felt like Violet’s. Somewhere in all that excitement I dropped a bombshell. I was burned out and didn’t want to be principal anymore, so I resigned to stay home with Violet.

places.title: Our Tampa babymoon

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah taking a sunny outdoor selfie in Tampa.
photos.caption: A Tampa afternoon with our littlest travel companion still on board.

places.story: Back home, my office was turning into a nursery. Down in Tampa we still looked like a couple on vacation, but by then every picture of the two of us had Violet in it, too.

places.title: Waco
places.story: Violet and I had made a few trips to see Grandma and Grandpa that fall, but Waco was our first real trip as a family of three. We went with Savannah’s family, checked out the Magnolia Market silos, and saw some of Waco. The B&B was questionable. The food, as usual, was worth talking about.

photos.alt: Andy, Savannah, baby Violet, and Savannah’s parents beneath the Miles to Magnolia sign in Waco.
photos.caption: Violet’s first trip to Magnolia, with Grandma and Grandpa.

places.title: Thanksgiving in Shawnee
places.story: For Thanksgiving we drove to Shawnee, Kansas, to see my Uncle Kent, Aunt Debbie, my cousin Stephanie, and Tanner, who’s now Stephanie’s husband. It was our first big road trip with Violet. Getting to spend the holiday together and bring her along for it made the drive worth it.

photos.alt: The family posing together with baby Violet while a dog sits in front of them.
photos.caption: Thanksgiving in Shawnee. Even the dog made the family photo.

places.title: A painting date

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah each holding a painted canvas with a blue sky.
photos.caption: Two canvases, two takes on the same sky.

places.story: In a year spent mostly at home with Violet, we made time for a painting date. We started with the same scene and came away with two different skies to hang up.

places.title: Violet turns one
places.story: We left in late May and came back in early June, visiting our families in North Carolina and at Cohutta Springs. In the middle of that trip we celebrated Violet’s first birthday. Somehow, a whole year had gone by since that last day of school.

photos.alt: Savannah helps Violet, in a tiny party hat, open a birthday present
photos.caption: Celebrating Violet’s first birthday.

places.title: Violet’s first trip to Canada
places.story: We went up to International Falls, crossed into Fort Frances, and drove about half an hour northeast. We stopped by the water with Violet. It’s still her only international trip so far.

photos.alt: Savannah holds Violet’s hands at the water’s edge
photos.caption: By the water northeast of Fort Frances, Ontario.

places.title: Christmas in North Carolina and Cohutta Springs

photos.alt: Violet holds a hairbrush in front of the Christmas tree
photos.caption: Christmas in Hendersonville, North Carolina.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah with Violet at Christmas 2019
photos.caption: Violet and her red Christmas bow.

photos.alt: Andy, Savannah, and Violet sitting together in front of a brick wall at Christmas
photos.caption: All three of us, with Violet right in the middle.

places.story: We spent Christmas with our families in North Carolina and at Cohutta Springs. Christmas Day was in Hendersonville.

places.title: Hunkering down with game nights
places.story: When COVID shut everything down, we decided the Bonjours would be our COVID friends. We hunkered down and spent a lot of time playing games together. The nights around the table gave us something to look forward to when there wasn’t much else on the calendar.

photos.alt: An open Dungeon Master’s screen, a Monster Manual, and a game map on a screen across the table.
photos.caption: Behind the Dungeon Master’s screen in 2021.

photos.alt: Savannah taking a selfie with friends and kids around a dining table.
photos.caption: Back around the table together in 2023.

places.title: An afternoon on the swings

photos.alt: Violet in a blue swing with an adult on the swing beside her
photos.caption: A May afternoon on the swings.

places.story: That spring we spent a lot of our time close to home. An afternoon on the swings with Violet counted as a pretty good outing.

places.title: A North Dakota trip for Kelly’s wedding
places.story: My parents came to visit that summer. We also took a trip with Savannah’s parents to Minot and Bottineau for her cousin Kelly’s wedding. Along the way we stopped for a picnic, visited the Scandinavian Heritage Park in Minot, and got lunch together. In a year when we spent so much time at home, it was good to have a wedding to celebrate with family.

photos.alt: Violet and an adult sitting at an outdoor picnic table with fruit and sandwiches.
photos.caption: A roadside picnic with Violet on the way to Kelly’s wedding.

photos.alt: Savannah with her arms around a bronze statue, with a windmill in the background.
photos.caption: Savannah made a new friend at Minot’s Scandinavian Heritage Park.

photos.alt: Andy taking a selfie while everyone sits around a restaurant table.
photos.caption: Lunch together in Minot after a morning out.

places.title: A date close to home
places.story: At the end of July, Savannah and I went on a date close to home. We’d spent plenty of time at home together that year, but getting out for a little time just the two of us still felt like an occasion.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah smiling together in a selfie
photos.caption: Just the two of us on our late-July date.

places.title: August in Orlando
places.story: We went to Orlando in August and made time for the coast, too. After so much time close to home, it was a welcome change of scenery.

photos.alt: Two kids crawling side by side across a living room floor
photos.caption: The kids crawling together on our August 2020 Florida trip.

places.title: A day at Bethune Beach
places.place: Mary McLeod Bethune Beach Park, Florida
places.story: On that August Florida trip we headed out to Mary McLeod Bethune Beach Park. It was good to trade the usual view from home for sand and ocean for a while.

photos.alt: Andy, Savannah, and Violet sitting together in beach chairs
photos.caption: A beach day at Mary McLeod Bethune Beach Park.

places.title: A September trip to the Minnesota Zoo
places.story: In September we took Violet to the Minnesota Zoo. It was a chance to get out together and let her see some animals up close.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah standing beside Violet in her stroller at the zoo
photos.caption: The three of us at the Minnesota Zoo.

photos.alt: Violet in pink rain boots standing at the edge of a puddle, with her reflection in the water.
photos.caption: Pink boots, deep puddle, and two Violets.

photos.alt: Violet holding two stuffed animals while sitting among fallen leaves.
photos.caption: Nobody gets left inside when there are fall leaves to sit in.

photos.alt: Violet reaching over to pet a dog sitting beside her on the couch.
photos.caption: The best seat on the couch is next to the dog.

photos.alt: Savannah holding Violet in a colorful hammock, both laughing.
photos.caption: November sunshine and a laugh with Mom.

places.title: Anniversary breakfast for two in Stillwater

photos.alt: Two breakfast plates on a tray with coffee and orange juice
photos.caption: Anniversary breakfast at a bed and breakfast in Stillwater.

places.story: For our anniversary, Savannah and I stayed at a bed and breakfast in Stillwater. Waking up to a tray of breakfast for two was a sweet way to celebrate.

places.title: Christmas at Cohutta Springs
places.story: That Christmas we headed south to spend the holiday with Savannah’s family at Cohutta Springs. After a quiet year at home, it was good to finish it together in Georgia.

photos.alt: Savannah and Violet opening a present together on the couch
photos.caption: Christmas morning at Cohutta Springs.

places.title: D&D every Saturday
places.story: With everything shut down, we didn’t have much else to do on Saturdays, so we played D&D. Every Saturday night. Years later, this is the whole crew together around one table.

photos.alt: The full D&D group gathered around a dining table with food.
photos.caption: Our Saturday-night D&D crew, all together in February 2026.

places.title: A spring visit to Hendersonville

photos.alt: Violet watches as her grandpa drives a riding mower with Savannah riding behind
photos.caption: Dad and Savannah on the mower in Hendersonville.

places.story: We went back to North Carolina that spring to see my family. Dad got the riding mower out, Savannah went along for the ride, and Violet got a front-row view from the yard.

places.title: A hike in Pisgah National Forest

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah smiling together on a wooded hiking trail
photos.caption: A spring hike in Pisgah National Forest.

places.story: Savannah and I got out for a hike in Pisgah National Forest while we were in North Carolina. A little time together out in the woods was a good way to spend a spring morning.

places.title: A hundred days together in Minnesota
places.story: Savannah’s parents came to Minnesota that spring and lived with us for a hundred days. We got to share the everyday parts of life with them, and Violet got a whole stretch of grandparent time.

places.title: Violet’s summer around the Twin Cities
places.place: Twin Cities and west metro, Minnesota

photos.alt: Violet in a white dress walking through a splash pad
photos.caption: A July splash-pad day.

photos.alt: Violet smiling while sitting on a rock in the shade
photos.caption: A shady spot to sit for a minute.

photos.alt: Violet wearing a pink helmet and riding a blue tricycle
photos.caption: Out for a ride.

places.story: We had so much fun with Violet that summer. We took her to playgrounds and swimming ponds, found places to splash, and spent as much time outside as we could. It was the kind of summer where an outing close to home could be the best part of the day.

places.title: Summer outings in Central Minnesota
places.story: A couple more pictures of Violet from that summer, including one with Mom among the flowers.

photos.alt: Violet smiling outdoors with a purple bow in her hair
photos.caption: Violet out and about in July.

photos.alt: Savannah and Violet sitting together on the grass in front of bright flowers
photos.caption: An August outing with Mom.

places.title: The Renaissance Festival with Violet

photos.alt: Violet standing beside a pirate figure at the Renaissance Festival
photos.caption: Violet and a pirate at the Renaissance Festival.

places.story: We kept our run of outings going into September with a trip to the Renaissance Festival. Violet even stopped for a picture with a pirate.

places.title: Dancing at Kelly’s wedding

photos.alt: Violet dancing hand in hand with a woman at the wedding reception
photos.caption: Violet on the dance floor at Kelly’s wedding in Omaha.

places.story: We went to Omaha in September for Savannah’s friend Kelly’s wedding. Violet made her way onto the dance floor, and watching her dance was one of my favorite parts of the night.

places.title: Disney and the beach with Violet

photos.alt: Violet grinning beside Savannah and Andy at Disney
photos.caption: All three of us at Disney.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah leaning in to kiss Violet at the beach
photos.caption: Kisses from both sides for our girl.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah standing with Violet where the waves meet the sand
photos.caption: An October evening by the water.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah holding Violet at the shoreline
photos.caption: The three of us by the ocean in October.

places.story: The three of us went to Disney, and we made time for the beach, too. There’s a photo of us kissing Violet from both sides with the ocean behind her. We love our girl so much. Getting to share these adventures with her was the best part of the trip.

places.title: A quiet Christmas in Forest Lake

photos.alt: Family sitting together on a couch beside a lit Christmas tree
photos.caption: Christmas with Savannah’s family in Forest Lake.

places.story: We kept Christmas low-key that year and stayed in Minnesota. We went to Savannah’s parents’ place in Forest Lake and spent the holiday with family. It was nice to have a Christmas without a long drive.

places.title: Max and Ellie at play
places.story: Max and Ellie were getting bigger, and by February they were both up at the activity table. Two little faces looking up at the same time was worth a picture.

photos.alt: Max and Ellie smiling together behind a colorful activity table
photos.caption: Two little faces at the activity table.

places.title: Violet’s dress-up outfit
places.story: Some of the best photos are the ones we get without going anywhere. This was one of Violet’s outfits, complete with a green hat and a whole lot of color.

photos.alt: Violet dressed in a green hat and layers of colorful clothes
photos.caption: Violet all dressed up at home.

places.title: March in Hendersonville

photos.alt: Andy, Savannah, and the three kids sitting together on a bench by spring flowers downtown
photos.caption: All five of us in downtown Hendersonville.

photos.alt: Violet standing behind Max and Ellie as the twins sit in the grass.
photos.caption: Violet and the twins out on the grass during our North Carolina trip.

photos.alt: Savannah and Andy leaning in for a selfie outdoors.
photos.caption: A little spring sunshine and a picture of just the two of us.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah smiling together in front of a brick wall
photos.caption: A photo of just the two of us on our March trip to North Carolina.

places.story: We went back to Hendersonville in March. We got a picture of all five of us downtown and one of Violet with the twins out on the grass. Savannah and I even got a couple of pictures of just the two of us, one outside and one in front of a brick wall.

places.title: Max and Ellie, cheek to cheek

photos.alt: Max and Ellie sitting close together on the carpet beside their toys.
photos.caption: A two-baby hug and a big grin.

places.title: A June afternoon outside
places.story: The twins were about to turn one. In the middle of that busy summer, I’m glad we took a picture of the two of us sitting outside at home.

photos.alt: Savannah and Andy smiling at an outdoor table
photos.caption: Savannah and me outside at home on a June afternoon.

places.title: The little things at home
places.story: August gave us two pictures that sum up life with the kids pretty well. In one, a little face is smiling out from an open cupboard. In the other, nap time wins right there at the high chair.

photos.alt: One of the twins smiling from inside an open kitchen cupboard
photos.caption: An unexpected place to sit.

photos.alt: One of the twins asleep at the high-chair tray beside some food
photos.caption: When nap time comes before the last bite.

places.title: A Dairy Queen stop near New Smyrna Beach
places.story: On our September trip, we stopped at a Dairy Queen near New Smyrna Beach. All five of us squeezed into a picture around the outdoor table.

photos.alt: Savannah taking a selfie with Andy and all three kids around an outdoor table
photos.caption: All five of us at Dairy Queen near New Smyrna Beach.

places.title: New Smyrna Beach

photos.alt: Andy, Savannah, and the three kids sitting on driftwood beside the ocean
photos.caption: All five of us at New Smyrna Beach.

places.story: We got back to New Smyrna Beach in September. We managed to get all five of us into one photo on a piece of driftwood, with the waves rolling in behind us.

places.title: Date night at home

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah standing together at home in red outfits
photos.caption: A fall date night at home.

places.story: One fall date night was right at home. With three little kids and a full house, it felt good to set aside an evening for just us.

places.title: Halloween with the kids
places.story: We got the kids together in costume for a Halloween photo. Violet had her witch hat, and the twins were bundled up in their costumes beside her.

photos.alt: Violet in a witch costume next to the twins in yellow and orange costumes
photos.caption: The kids dressed up for Halloween.

places.title: Ten years married
places.story: Ten years since that wedding day in 2013. We’d gone from planning a wedding and flying to New Zealand to raising Violet, Max, and Ellie. For our tenth anniversary date night, we got out the paint and really enjoyed making art together. 😉 The days are a lot louder now, and I love the life we’ve made together. Happy ten years, Savannah.

photos.alt: An abstract painting with black brushstrokes and splatters on a light canvas
photos.caption: The art we made on our tenth-anniversary date night. 😉

photos.alt: Savannah and Andy walking together outside in their wedding clothes
photos.caption: Back where it started, on our 2013 wedding day in Middletown, California.

places.title: Christmas at my parents’ place
places.story: We spent Christmas with my parents in Hendersonville. There was a ride on a toy tractor, an outing where we looked through wooden trays together, and a bath that Ellie decided wasn’t over yet. We’d already gotten her out and into her jammies when she climbed right back in.

photos.alt: One of the twins sitting on a green ride-on tractor in the yard
photos.caption: A tractor ride at my parents’ place.

photos.alt: Violet and family gathered around wooden trays
photos.caption: Out together the day after Christmas.

photos.alt: Ellie back in the bathtub in her pajamas with colorful bath toys.
photos.caption: We got Ellie out and into her jammies. She got right back in.

places.title: Off on our Caribbean cruise
places.story: Our cruise adventure started with a flight out of the Twin Cities. We got a picture of the two of us together before we headed south.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah smiling in their airplane seats
photos.caption: The flight out to start our cruise.

places.title: Taking it easy at Half Moon Cay
places.story: We got off the ship for a stop at Half Moon Cay and took some time to sit back and enjoy the sunshine.

photos.alt: Savannah in sunglasses relaxing on a waterfront lounge seat
photos.caption: A sunny stop at Half Moon Cay.

places.title: A day on Grand Turk
places.story: We had time to relax on Grand Turk, and we got a few photos together by the water. My favorite is the one where we stopped for a kiss with the sky behind us.

photos.caption: A kiss on the shore of Grand Turk.

photos.alt: Savannah reclining in a lounge chair on Grand Turk
photos.caption: Taking it easy on Grand Turk.

photos.alt: Savannah and Andy dressed up on a boardwalk overlooking the ocean

places.title: Our stop in Aruba
places.story: We made it to Aruba near the end of January and stopped for a picture at the I Love Aruba sign.

photos.caption: Our stop in Aruba.

photos.alt: Andy and Savannah standing together in front of greenery in San Diego.

places.story: A few months after the cruise, Savannah and I got some April sunshine in San Diego. I like this picture of us tucked in close with green leaves filling the frame behind us.

places.story: It feels like we were just getting Violet ready for her first day of Pre-K at MCA. Now here she was at kindergarten graduation, in a blue cap, with two generations of family lined up behind her.

photos.alt: Two of the kids leaning in close on a couch.

places.story: We loaded the five of us into the van and drove down to my parents’ place near Hendersonville. We spent three days with them before getting back in the van for Florida. Nearly 50 hours of driving by the time we got home, with two three-year-olds along for all of it. That counts as a big trip in our book.

places.title: Fifty years and a family reunion

places.story: From North Carolina we drove to Orlando for the Carlson family reunion and to celebrate my parents’ 50th wedding anniversary. We got to spend time with family and the kids had plenty of company. The twins even made it into a picture with the reunion sign.

places.story: On the way back, we drove to Tennessee to see the Bonjours. The kids got time to play together before we piled back into the van for the last stretch home. It was a good way to end the trip.

photos.caption: Violet ready for her Splash & Dash, green swim cap and all.

places.story: Violet and I both got to race in Maple Grove. She did the Splash & Dash, and I did the triathlon. My favorite bit was getting a picture with both of our medals afterward.

places.story: We headed way up north to camp for a friend’s birthday. By evening we were down on the rocks by the lake, with camp chairs, snacks, and a sunset worth staying out for.

places.title: Shelina’s birthday
places.story: That September, Savannah and I got dressed up to celebrate our friend Shelina’s birthday. Somewhere in the evening we stopped long enough to get this picture of the two of us.

photos.alt: Savannah and Andy posing in dress clothes outdoors.
photos.caption: Dressed up for Shelina’s birthday.

places.title: The Bucs win the Super Bowl!
places.story: As a diehard Bucs fan, this was a big day for me. Tampa Bay won Super Bowl LV, and I got to celebrate it with Savannah and Violet. I think the grin in this picture says it all.

photos.alt: Andy, Savannah, and Violet smiling in Bucs colors.
photos.caption: Celebrating a Super Bowl win with my favorite Bucs fans.

photos.caption: A May picnic north of the Twin Cities.

places.title: Meet Oliver
places.story: Savannah got Oliver in 2010. He was a loving cat, with one small exception. Your ears were fair game.

photos.alt: Oliver, a striped tabby, sleeping with his face tucked against his paw.
photos.caption: A sweetheart when your ears were out of reach.
